tagline: An AI-assisted research and answer workflow that can help explore questions and locate sources.

pros: Can be evaluated for quickly exploring a question and finding candidate sources to inspect.
Source links provide a path for checking claims against original material when available.
Useful trial tasks include research synthesis, follow-up questions and comparing source quality.
A source-checking rubric can make research reviews more reproducible.
A pilot can reveal whether citations support the generated claims.
cons: A citation may not support every sentence or may omit important context; verify it directly.
Generated summaries can contain errors, missing caveats or stale information.
Review privacy, retention, access and enterprise data terms before entering confidential material.

content.title: Research workflow
content.body: Begin with a question that has a verifiable answer and define what evidence would count. Use the tool to discover sources and identify subquestions, then open the original sources rather than treating a generated summary as the final authority.

content.title: Check citations and claims
content.body: For each material claim, follow the citation, confirm that the page exists, inspect the relevant passage and record the publication date. Distinguish a primary source such as documentation or a study from commentary that repeats someone else's claim.

content.title: Compare source coverage
content.body: Run a repeatable research task and note which credible sources are included, omitted or mischaracterized. Check whether the answer reflects disagreement, uncertainty, geography and time period. A long list of citations is not a substitute for relevant evidence.

content.title: Use for writing and synthesis
content.body: Ask for a structured outline or comparison, then check every number, quotation, named entity and conclusion. Keep notes about what was independently verified and rewrite the synthesis in your own words with links to original sources.

content.title: Privacy and responsible use
content.body: Before submitting internal documents or personal data, review the current product's data controls, retention and workspace terms. Apply the same confidentiality rules used for other external services and avoid pasting secrets or regulated data without approval.

content.title: Decision rule
content.body: Use AI-assisted research to accelerate discovery and organize questions, not to remove fact-checking. For legal, medical, financial, security or other high-impact decisions, consult authoritative sources and qualified professionals.

content.title: Research test case
content.body: Choose a question with a known primary source and at least one important caveat. Ask the tool for a summary, then verify each material claim by opening the cited page and locating the supporting passage. Record missing sources, unsupported statements, publication dates and whether the answer distinguishes evidence from interpretation.

content.title: Source-quality rubric
content.body: Score source authority, relevance, recency, directness and independence. A government document, official product specification or original study may be stronger evidence for a specific claim than a secondary summary. When credible sources disagree, preserve the disagreement rather than asking the model to invent certainty.

content.title: Decision record
content.body: Keep the original research question, important source links, checked claims and unresolved uncertainty. Treat the tool as a discovery and synthesis aid, not the final source of truth. For high-impact decisions, consult authoritative primary sources and qualified professionals and do not submit confidential information unless approved.

faqs.question: Who should evaluate Perplexity?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Perplexity when its primary workflow matches a documented requirement. Test a representative task and verify current capabilities and limits directly with the vendor.

faqs.question: How should a team test Perplexity?
faqs.answer: Use the same real input, expected outcome and acceptance criteria each time. Record pass, partial pass, fail or unknown, including setup time, manual work and failure handling.

faqs.question: Which limitations should be checked in Perplexity?
faqs.answer: Check the exact plan, integrations, permissions, export, data retention, recovery and ongoing administration. Treat untested or undocumented capabilities as unknown until confirmed.

faqs.question: Are Perplexity prices and ratings independently verified here?
faqs.answer: No. Current prices, plan limits and independent ratings are not verified in this review. Check official documentation and obtain a dated quote before purchase.

faqs.question: What should be confirmed before adopting Perplexity?
faqs.answer: Confirm the core workflow, access controls, integrations, data export, account offboarding, support responsibilities and renewal terms. Assign an owner for the implementation and ongoing review.

author: Marcus Rivera
learningCurve: Moderate — expect 1-3 days to become productive
whoShouldUse: People researching unfamiliar topics, comparing options, or looking for answers with linked sources can evaluate Perplexity as a search and research assistant. Test queries from your own work, open the cited sources, and check whether the answer distinguishes sourced facts from synthesis or uncertainty.
whoShouldNotUse: Do not treat generated summaries or citations as automatically correct: open sources and verify important claims yourself. Avoid relying on it as the sole authority for high-impact decisions, and review current data-use and privacy terms before entering confidential material.
